findings.title: src/jarvis_foundry/kernel/secrets.py is gitignored and would be silently omitted from the R4 commit
findings.reproduction: .gitignore line 10 'secrets.*' matches src/jarvis_foundry/kernel/secrets.py (git check-ignore confirms). git status --porcelain -uall lists 21 untracked kernel files while 22 kernel files exist on disk; the 22nd file is secrets.py. Directory-based ruff format on the kernel counts 21 files (52 total across R4 roots) while the gate scripts pass an explicit 53-file list and report 53.
findings.invariant: Every mandatory R4 kernel module must be promotable from the worktree to the commit/clean checkout.
findings.adjudication: No current gate criterion failed: artifact manifest hashes match disk and gate scripts use explicit file lists. But a normal 'git add src/jarvis_foundry/kernel' by root would silently exclude secrets.py, producing an incomplete committed kernel and broken focused tests on a clean clone. Root must force-add the file or amend .gitignore (e.g., '!src/jarvis_foundry/kernel/secrets.py') before committing R4. This is a new defect requiring root action.

findings.title: Read-only hardening narrows but does not close round-1 R4-V-001: Ledger.connect()/transaction() remain public writable handles
findings.reproduction: Independent probe on isolated temp DBs: with ledger.connect() as c: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS ledger_events_no_update succeeded, then UPDATE ledger_events SET payload='{}' succeeded. With ledger.transaction(): DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS ledger_events_no_delete succeeded, then DELETE succeeded. ledger.read_connection() refused all four mutations with OperationalError 'attempt to write a readonly database'. test_public_connect_handle_is_read_only covers only read_connection(); frozen_mutants.json contains no mutant for the mode=ro hardening.
findings.invariant: Canonical ledger state must not be mutable by any caller outside kernel-internal append/init.
findings.adjudication: The claimed hardening (public read handles are read-only; public reads cannot mutate) is verified TRUE. connect()/transaction() remain writable and are public methods with no access control, so round-1 recommendation 'restrict connect()/transaction() to kernel-internal use or add a schema-owner guard' is still open. Consistent with round-1 adjudication, this is not a criterion failure because LedgerPort does not expose them, architecture gate is clean, and no non-kernel source imports kernel state. Recorded as residual risk; a follow-up hardening should privatize or guard connect()/transaction().
